title: Does a trained verifier convert extra coverage into accuracy?
VERDICT: MATCHED BUDGET (the number that answers the question): vqa_rad_open -0.0309 going from an 8-sample to a 16-sample pool on identical questions -- doubling the sampling budget makes it WORSE. Within-pool subsampling separately shows the verifier converting 72.6% of the oracle gain from N=2 to N=16, but that curve handicaps small N on coverage and does NOT license spending more samples. The coverage attack fails: extra candidates make ranking harder faster than extra coverage helps, which is the same effect the union-pool and pruning experiments found from the other two directions.
two_readings_note: The within-pool N curve rises and the matched-budget comparison falls. They are not in conflict: subsampling N from a fixed 16-sample pool removes coverage that the pool already paid for, so small N is handicapped. Only the matched comparison of two real generation runs answers 'should we sample more'.
